text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The government and leaders of the three main trade unions seem near to an agreement over the 1997 budget, even if unions do not rule out a national mobilisation until the next meeting, scheduled by November 12, has taken place (all).
* Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni says there will be no pension cut in 1997 (all).

* In a conference about "Ethics and the economy" Fiat former chairman Giovanni Agnelli says "the welfare state is collapsing" and calls for "brave measures" from the government. Governor of the Bank of Italy Antonio Fazio says "it is time to cut public expenditure" (all).
* PDS leader Massimo D'Alema is due to meet today Freedom alliance leaders to discuss the set-up of the bicameral commission for constitutional reforms (all).
* In an interview, Treasury minister Ciampi says Italy today does "respect European criteria for inflation and interest rates. Now we must work on the deficit" (Corriere della Sera).
* Merchant bank Mediobanca says it has been kept out from privatisations (all).
* The issue of Italian post office bonds has been suspended in the face of heavy demand, especially by foreign banks such as Nomura.(all)
* The Treasury is said to be planning a split in two parts of state holding company Iri (Sole 24 Ore).
* An extraordinary shareholders meeting of Italian state telecoms holding Stet formally approved plans to spin off its telephone directory publishing unit Seat (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
